chapter_title: Concerning the Alms, that [ ... ] life in the Church.
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by institutional/almsgiving material about the holy church and catechumens (pastoral/editorial extension). The oldest cosmological teaching appears mainly in ¶7–10, where the ascent of the living soul through the sun and moon and the resting of the light-givers in the Land of Light is described entirely within the cosmic system (no church application).

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic hagiographic opening scene-setting (“Once again… the enlightener… He says to his disciples”).
Institutional polemic and alms discipline (sects, catechumens, holy church, commandments of alms). Cosmos→institution mapping/application dominates.
Defines the church ‘in two forms’ (brothers/sisters) and treats alms as redeemed through the church—operational ecclesial register, not cosmic system description.
Editorial extension in institutional terms (church as doorway, depends on catechumens). This is church logistics/application rather than cosmological mechanism.

Although cast as a simile (earth/tree/gardener), it is explicitly keyed to the ‘assembly of catechumens’; the correspondence is used to point to institutional roles, so it is not the pre-compilation substrate.
Direct church/catechumen dependency teaching (“place wherein there are no catechumens…”). Pattern-mimicking extension of the simile into institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: Likewise this [liv]ing sou[l] that today is set in mixture; for it wishes to [as]cend and go to the house of its people, but it kn[ow[s a]nd understands that it has no open door in all the powers of heaven and earth. For they are its oppression that [ ... ] it everywhere. Indeed, it has no open door except the sun and the moon themselves, the light-givers of the heavens [ ... / ... ] they become the place of rest for it. And they become a door that opens for it [in] the coming forth, and (the soul) comes out through them to the country of the household of i[ts] people.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological mechanics (mixture; ascent; ‘open door’; sun and moon as light-givers/vehicles). Despite the word ‘today’, the mapping remains cosmos→cosmos with no ecclesial application.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, further in, also the light-givers of the heavens have no place of rest amongst all the powers of heaven; except for the lan[d] of light, that has indeed been theirs for ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: System-internal hierarchy: light-givers’ resting-place defined only by cosmic domains (powers of heaven; Land of Light).

paragraphs.core_text: So, thus the living soul is purified of all afflictions; and they provide a rest for it, and open a door that opens to the house [of] its people.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the same cosmological process description (purification/rest/door) without institutional referents.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, it is the case that the land of lig[ht] will become the final receiver for the light-givers of [the] heavens, and they will rest themselves therein and rule in it [for] ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic eschatological settling: Land of Light as ‘final receiver’ for the light-givers—structural, non-exhortative, non-citing voice.
Explicit institutional analogy returns (church ↔ alms of catechumens), concluding with shared ‘place of rest’—a cosmos→church application paragraph rather than core cosmology.
